Hi Dina —

Apologies for the short delay — attached is a short answer set (spreadsheet) and a dataflow diagram. Answers below in the format you requested. If you'd like, we can convert this into a single-page checklist for your vendor intake form.

1) Prefix / KV cache persistence
- Behavior: By default, Redwood’s prefix and KV caches are in-memory only on serving nodes and are not persisted to customer-accessible long-term storage.
- Replication: Within a cluster, caches may be mirrored across GPUs for fast failover, but that replication is within the same region/availability zone unless a cross-region failover is explicitly configured at account setup.
- Exception: Customers on Dedicated or Private deployments may opt into local persistence for performance; Hosted customers are in-memory by default.

2) Default TTLs and configurability
- Default values (Hosted):
  • Prefix cache (token-level prefix caching): 30 seconds
  • KV cache (model KV/attention cache): ephemeral for session; cleared on session termination or model swap
  • Response cache (only used for deterministic handlers; opt-in): 5 minutes
- Configurability: All TTLs above are configurable for enterprise Hosted customers via account policy. We expose these settings in our console or via an API for account admins.

3) Request / response logs
- Default retention (Hosted): 30 days for request metadata and full request/response payloads (where enabled).
- Account controls: Enterprise accounts can request logging be disabled (no request/response payloads stored) — metadata for billing and telemetry is still retained with minimal retention by default (30 days) unless a stricter SLA is negotiated.
- Export: Logs can be exported via secure S3 dump with MFA and signed URL.

4) Deletion process & proof artifacts
- Step 1 (hot removal): When a deletion/erasure request is issued, we immediately stop serving any cached entries for the affected tenant and remove in-memory caches.
- Step 2 (index/metadata mark): We mark records in our indices and queue them for asynchronous purge.
- Step 3 (persistent store purge): Logs and persisted artifacts (if any) are deleted from object storage per the account retention policy. Standard hosted deletion pipeline processes queued deletes within 7–30 days depending on data class and shard backlog.
- Step 4 (backups): Backups are subject to retention windows. For Hosted customers, snapshots are retained up to 90 days; deletion requests trigger inclusion of identifiers in the next backup purge cycle (no longer than 90 days).
- Proof of deletion: We provide a deletion certificate (timestamped) listing identifiers removed and the purge job id. For enterprise contracts, we can provide quarterly deletion attestations.

5) Regional routing and cross-region behavior
- Pinning: Hosted API customers can request region pinning (US, EU, APAC). When pinned to US, we ensure primary serving and persistent stores are located in a US region.
- Fallbacks: We do not cross-region fallback for pinned accounts under normal operation. Cross-region failover is opt-in and requires explicit configuration and SSO approvals.
- Edge cases: Temporary replication for health-check failovers may occur in colocated regions; we will disclose these cases in the account manifest.

6) Maintenance / edge cases
- Maintenance windows or emergency failovers may necessitate short-lived replication; we notify account admins and log any cross-region access.
- For high-privacy customers, we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments to avoid any possibility of transient cross-region copies.
